body: From the video using the same type of node it's pretty hard to tell exactly what happens, could you rename the node you are moving to make it more illustrative?

> When trying to move a node in the SceneTree to the last place, the dragged node will always become a child of the last expanded parent in the list. That's intended / that's how it is currently implemented. >Dragging left and right to place as a peer does not work, like it does for entries higher in the list, albeit very unpredictably. Dragging left/right doesn't change anything, drop sections/zones are vertical only. In the video (around `0:23` timestamp) you're dragging left/right on the edge between two items, while doing so the cursor moves between bottom drop section of the item above, and the top drop section of the item below. See [`Tree.DropModeFlags` enum docs](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_tree.html#enum-tree-dropmodeflags). The Tree in the editor's Scene dock has both `DROP_MODE_ON_ITEM` and `DROP_MODE_INBETWEEN` enabled, meaning each item there has 3 drop sections (percentages are approx because internally integers are used for section calculations): - ~25% top area - ~50% middle area - ~25% bottom area Here's visualization using custom EditorPlugin (and `interface/theme/spacing_preset` editor setting set to `Spacious`):
EditorPlugin adding debug draw shown beolw (click to expand)

```gdscript @tool extends EditorPlugin var drawer: TreeDropSectionsDrawer func _enter_tree() -> void: var base_control: Control = EditorInterface.get_base_control() var scene_tree_editor: Control = base_control.find_children("", "SceneTreeEditor", true, false)[0] var tree: Tree = scene_tree_editor.find_children("", "Tree", true, false)[0] drawer = TreeDropSectionsDrawer.new() drawer.tree = tree tree.add_child(drawer) func _exit_tree() -> void: drawer.queue_free() class TreeDropSectionsDrawer: extends Node2D var tree: Tree func _ready() -> void: z_index = RenderingServer.CANVAS_ITEM_Z_MAX func _process(delta: float) -> void: queue_redraw() func _draw() -> void: if not is_instance_valid(tree): return var mouse_position: Vector2 = tree.get_local_mouse_position() var hovered_item: TreeItem = tree.get_item_at_position(mouse_position) if not is_instance_valid(hovered_item): return var item_rect: Rect2 = tree.get_item_area_rect(hovered_item) var h: int = item_rect.size.y # Internally it uses ints for calculations. var section_top_rect: Rect2 = item_rect section_top_rect.size.y = h / 4 var section_bottom_rect: Rect2 = item_rect section_bottom_rect.position.y += h * 3 / 4 section_bottom_rect.end.y = item_rect.end.y var section_middle_rect: Rect2 = item_rect section_middle_rect.position.y = section_top_rect.end.y section_middle_rect.end.y = section_bottom_rect.position.y #draw_set_transform_matrix(global_transform.affine_inverse() * tree.get_global_transform()) draw_rect(section_top_rect, Color(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.302)) draw_rect(section_middle_rect, Color(0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.302)) draw_rect(section_bottom_rect, Color(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.302)) #draw_rect(tree.get_item_area_rect(hovered_item, 0), Color(1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.302)) ```

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12283ccc-184b-440a-968c-1164335e22e3 --- So there's no bug in here. If you're suggesting it should behave differently in the "left part of the bottom section": https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8a719951-0fab-4854-bf0e-a23346806d92 then it's a subject for [a proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals). See also: - https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/3201

Thank you for the explanation.

I'm going to be attempting to implement something a little more intuitive, akin to how it is done in Sketch and other vector design software. Where left-right movement in the gutter between nodes determines parent, while still being able to drag on top of nodes to child to them directly.
